messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: streaming.sse.p99_latency > SLO threshold in prod eu-west-1. paging oncall. severity: SEV3. links: https://ops.redwood/alerts/7554321987 :rotating_light:
anna: acked, I'm oncall. grabbing logs now. what's the p95/p99 numbers?
incident-bot: p95 = 420ms, p99 = 3.1s on SSE chunking, spike started 10:03 UTC. error rate low; root cause likely stalls/delayed chunks.
anna: thanks. leo, maya — can you join? I need quick confirmation if this is proxy-layer or runtime-level.
leo: joining. saw a pattern earlier where proxy keepalive resets coincided with stall windows. will pull proxy metrics.
maya: joining. I'll tail runtime logs for KV cache/backpressure.
rob: I'm checking the ingress pool (nginx-proxy-*) — there are a bunch of `TIME_WAIT` and some keepalive closes around the event.
kevin: customer-success-beth pinged — one enterprise tenant reported UI 'stalls' and reconnects around 10:05. not a full outage but bad UX.
customer-success-beth: Customer reported intermittent long spinner. They pasted a minimal trace: multiple `HTTP/2 RST_STREAM` after long idle.
anna: OK hypothesis: proxy keepalive timeouts + client slow consumers => buffered data not flushed, leads to backend KV/cache pressure and tail latency. steps: 1) confirm proxy timeouts and TCP resets; 2) check client-side windowing/backpressure; 3) apply short-term mitigation (bump proxy keepalive, enable aggressive chunk flush), 4) scale proxy pool.
leo: proxy metrics show a spike in `upstream_response_time` and `proxy_write_timeout` around 10:03-10:07. config on edges shows keepalive 30s, but we have older SDKs with lower window sizes.
maya: runtime traces: a few long GC pauses on one model-host but mostly not across the fleet. tail latency correlates with proxy write backpressure rather than model compute.
rob: confirmed `nginx` logs: repeated `client closed connection while sending to upstream` and `upstream prematurely closed connection` around the window.
anna: evidence leans proxy -> client backpressure. mitigation options: A) temporarily increase proxy keepalive and proxy buffer flush interval; B) increase proxy pool size; C) enable immediate fallback routing to dedicated cluster for affected tenant; D) ask customer to upgrade SDK (longer-term).
kevin: CS asks for minimal disruption. they prefer no redirect if possible. recommend A + B now.
leo: rolling config change to proxy will be quick. I'll push a conservative change: keepalive 30s -> 90s and reduce `proxy_buffering` to `off` for SSE routes.
maya: I'll enable an HTTP flush on the runtime side for SSE endpoints (small change to server config) to ensure we flush early chunks and avoid large buffers.
anna: good. also increase proxy pool by 20% to handle transient load. rob/leo do that increment.
rob: scaling proxy pool now — adding 6 instances behind LB. ETA ~2m.
leo: applying keepalive/proxy_buffering change to canary (10%): `kubectl apply -f ingress-proxy-sse-canary.yaml` and watching.
leo: canary looks good, no 5xx. latency for SSE chunks improved in canary: p99 dropped from 3.1s -> 700ms for canary hosts.
anna: good signal. roll to 50% then 100% if stable. rob: confirm new instances up?
rob: new proxies healthy in LB. scaling done.
kevin: customer seeing improvement in session that was stuck — CS reports spinner cleared within 20s after their retry.
customer-success-beth: customer confirms they're seeing fewer stalls, still some slow ones but much better.
leo: rolling to 50% now. monitoring errors and p99.
maya: runtime flush change applied to SSE service in eu-west-1 - small config toggle. no regressions in unit tests.
anna: monitoring dashboards — p95 back to 180ms, p99 ~ 820ms. error rate unchanged. good.
incident-bot: UPDATE: paging note — reduced severity to SEV4 because impact is degraded UX for some customers but partial mitigation applied.
anna: writing a short timeline for handoff. please annotate any follow-ups you want on rotation.
leo: follow-up: need an ingress change in prod to make `proxy_buffering: off` default for all streaming routes and add a config flag to opt-in for older SDKs.
maya: follow-up: add a runtime metric for 'flush-latency' (time between chunk ready -> first byte on wire) so we can detect buffering origin in future.
rob: follow-up: investigate TCP `TIME_WAIT` and ephemeral port exhaustion in proxy autoscaling path; maybe tune ephemeral port reuse.
kevin: CS follow-up: advise customer of mitigation and recommend SDK upgrade to 1.4.2 which has fixed smaller window handling.
anna: handoff: I'm on for 15 more minutes, then handing to leo (next oncall). leo, please own the post-mortem actions and watch the canary rollback window for 2 hours.
leo: ack. I'll keep an eye for 2 hours and file the incident ticket with action items.
anna: thanks team. quick notes for incident ticket: root cause = proxy buffering + client slow-consumer behavior leading to stalled SSE chunk delivery; contributing factors = default `proxy_buffering` enabled for SSE routes, older mobile SDK with small HTTP/2 window; mitigations = bumped keepalive, disabled proxy_buffering for SSE routes, enabled runtime chunk flush, scaled proxy pool; next steps = make streaming route defaults safer, add flush-latency metric, customer outreach.
customer-success-beth: customer appreciative of quick response. wants ETA for SDK guidance.
leo: filing ticket now: https://ops.redwood/incidents/7554321987-postmortem — will include logs and metric graphs.
anna: handing off now to leo. I'll be reachable if anything flares. thanks. :thumbsup:
leo: thanks anna — taking over. leaving a short note in #oncall-handoff.
incident-bot: HANDOFF: 7554321987 assigned to leo. next update required by +2h or earlier if regression observed.
